newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-KWAN INSPIRED BY HAMILTON.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-KWAN INSPIRED BY HAMILTON.

text.p: Michelle Kwan turned for inspiration to ailing former Olympic men's figure skating champion Scott Hamilton and recovered her self-respect on Saturday.
Kwan disclosed after moving from fourth to second place behind Tara Lipinski that she had thought a lot about Hamilton, who was diagnosed this week as sufering from testicular cancer.
"I thought of Scott and that really put things in perspective. Here we are competing and there he is fighting for his life," she said.
The 1984 Olympic champion, 38, has begun chemotherapy treatment in an effort to beat the illness.

Kwan fell just short of retaining the title she won so spectacularly last year despite her best performance in the past month, during which she lost her U.S. National and Champions Series titles to Lipinski.
"It's a wonderful feeling to fly again," she said.
"I've been skating like a scared chicken, but I hope I've killed it off now.
"Instead of feeling like I had to win, I wanted to have fun today. I've learned a lesson this year.
"I enjoyed skating a lot more today."
Coach Frank Carroll said Kwan had learned a lesson.
"When you're reigning champion, you still have to fight to retain your title. It's a whole new battle.
"At the back of her mind she was still thinking she was champion," he said.
